newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures rally as rate fears ease.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures rally as rate fears ease.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended higher on Wednesday after dealers reassessed the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) latest tankan survey of corporate sentiment.

The tankan showed sentiment improving among big Japanese manufacturers, non-manufacturers more wary, but crucially gave no reason for the BOJ to tighten monetary policy in the short-term, dealers said.

"It suggests there will not be higher rates, at least for the next quarter," said one Singapore dealer. "There were worries the BOJ might follow the Fed and raise interest rates to maintain the spread."
The benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract closed 255 points higher at 18,085, after earlier dropping to an intra-day low of 17,705 points.
"It is good that it is above 18,000 at the close. It shows that it is building a bottom," said a dealer who follows technical charts closely.
He said the upside resistance was still at 18,300 and above that at 18,550 with support at 17,800 points.
"The 18,000 mark is not a very strong support," he said. "But 17,800 must hold if the market is to consolidate."
